# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 30 (Bu-Vb Np30)

**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 30
**Title (English, from literature):** Diverting an offering intended for the Sangha

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pariṇata Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 30) constitutes the thirtieth rule in the Nissaggiya Pācittiya section of the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule addresses the misdirection of communal property: a monk who deliberately diverts to his personal possession an offering originally designated for the Saṅgha (Order) incurs an offense requiring the relinquishment of the acquired item and confession of the transgression. A modern English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Computational text-reuse analysis confirms significant Pali-internal shared material, primarily with Bu-Vb Pc82 (§1.1–2.13 shared with §1.1–2.1.12), the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, and sub-commentarial treatises such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*, alongside formulaic overlaps with various other Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments generated by DharmaNexus also map sections of the rule to Sanskrit Prātimokṣasūtra texts and Tibetan commentaries, including the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104) and *Pratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4107) [DharmaNexus]. No citations or discussions of this rule were recovered from the provided secondary literature corpus.
